newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - US stocks seen locked in trading range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - US stocks seen locked in trading range.

text.p: U.S. stocks are locked in a trading range and any gains Friday are unlikely to break the pattern, technical analysts said.
Citing factors including high bullish investor sentiment, chartists see the Dow Industrials trading in a 6600-7000 range for at least the rest of the month.
"My belief is we're going to have difficulty at 6950," said Peter Green, vice president of technical research at Gruntal & Co. "I think it's going to take a while to break out to the upside."
At the end of January, Investors Intelligence's sentiment indicators showed 54 percent bullish and 27 percent bearish.

Fahnestock's director of investment strategy Joseph Barthel said in a report that the last time similar readings appeared was in May 1992, and the market then developed an 8.5 percent trading range that lasted seven months.

"While I continue to suspect that the DJIA (Dow Jones Industrial Average) should move up into the 7000 area, I also believe that a prolonged trading range environment is likely to develop once the DJIA approaches this critical resistance area," Barthel said.
Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities, said that in addition to the sentiment readings, he was keeping a close eye on utility stock indexes.
Utilities remain a good forecaster of the direction of the bond market, and further weakness there would further sap stocks' ability to drive out of their range, he said.

Utilities tested their January lows on Thursday. If the December low, at about 227 on the Dow utility index, is broken, "you're looking at a much more mixed picture on the direction of interest rates," Tower said.
The Dow untility index was down one at 228 Friday afternoon.
Helped by market-friendly January jobs data, the 30-year Treasury bond was up 10/32 to yield 6.73 percent.
Friday's action will be a key indicator of the near-term, analysts said.

Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities, said indicators that showed stocks in overbought positions in late January are now showing slight oversold readings, a bullish sign. But Wall Street stocks need to support any advance
Friday with large volume and above-average market breadth, he said.
"How we finish up today is another important clue in the short-term picture," Nie said.
In afternoon trading, gainers led losers by a seven to five ratio on the New York Stock Exchange, on active volume of about 410 million shares.
